To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the IFG, IPL, basal ganglia, anterior lobe of cerebellum, and parahippocampus are neuroanatomical predictors of individual differences on measures of divergent thinking and creative behaviour and achievement.

greater creativity is predicted by features of both the default mode network (DMN) and executive control network (ECN) as indexed by functional connectivity, and that the ECN-DMN connection, in turn, is predicted by white matter integrity in the superior longitudinal fascicle.
the inferior frontal gyrushas a key role in the cognitive neurobiology of creativity, and that the inferior parietal lobehas a key role, too.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cognitive neuroscience of creativity and the role of executive function in creative ideation.
the cognitive and neural bases of individual differences in creative ability.
understanding the neurobiological basis of human creativity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the IFG, IPL, and basal ganglia are reliable predictors of individual differences across a variety of measures of creativity, and that the parahippoccampal gyrus and anterior lobe of cerebellum may also be reliable predictors.
creativity is not associated with any single neuroanatomical feature, but rather with the interaction between a number of different neuroanatomical features.

the neuroimaging of human creativity has not yet reached the level of reliability required for the identification of a neural signature for creativity, although some promising candidates have emerged.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neural correlates of creativity are not yet clear.
the most reliable neuroimaging predictors of creative thinking are those related to the executive control network and the default mode network.
creativity is associated with the executive modulation of the default mode network, and that the basal ganglia, cerebellum, and medial temporal lobe are also important.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neuroimaging correlates of creativity are not as diverse as previously thought, but instead, a few key regions and networks are consistently implicated across different neuroimaging modalites and measures of creativity.
the neural correlates of individual creativity are likely to vary as a function of the specific task used to measure it.

, although creativity has been associated with a wide range of neuroimaging predictors in past studies, only a subset of these predictors have been reliably replicated across multiple samples, and these may represent a subset of neural correlates that have particular promise for future study.
